ch02.title: Boss battle: The Police Station Confession
ch02.scenario: X is accused of robbery. While in police custody, X tells the investigating officer, with no Magistrate present, that he took the money. At trial the prosecution wants to prove this.

questions.question: Which section most directly bars proving this statement against X?
questions.explanation: s.25: no confession made to a police-officer shall be proved against a person accused of any offence.

questions.question: If X had made it in police custody, what does s.26 additionally require for it to be proved?
questions.explanation: s.26: unless made in the immediate presence of a Magistrate.

questions.question: If an officer of authority had promised X leniency in reference to the charge, which section would make the confession irrelevant in a criminal proceeding?
questions.explanation: s.24 covers inducement, threat or promise from a person in authority.

ch03.title: Boss battle: The Last Words
ch03.scenario: V is fatally injured and, before dying, tells a neighbour who attacked him and how. V did not say he expected to die. The cause of V's death is in question at the trial.

questions.question: Which provision may make V's statement relevant?
questions.explanation: s.32(1): statement as to the cause of death or circumstances of the transaction that resulted in death.

questions.question: Does the absence of any expectation of death make the statement irrelevant?
options: No - relevant whether or not under expectation of death
Only if a Magistrate recorded it
questions.explanation: The text of s.32(1) says so expressly.

ch07.title: Boss battle: The Ticketless Traveller
ch07.scenario: A sues B for land B possesses, claiming it passed to A under a will. Separately, C is charged with travelling by rail without a ticket.

questions.question: In A's suit, on whom is the burden (if no evidence were given by either side B keeps possession)?
questions.explanation: s.102 illustration (a): B would retain possession, so the burden is on A.

questions.question: Who must prove C had a ticket?

ch08.title: Boss battle: The Land Sale
ch08.scenario: A intentionally and falsely leads B to believe certain land is A's, and B buys and pays for it. The land later becomes A's property and A sues B to recover it.

questions.question: Which principle prevents A from denying that the land was his to sell?
